3. Prosecution case in short 15 that R. S. Plot No. 115 of Monza Paschim Solashahar; P.S. Panchlaish, District Chittagong, was originally recorded as Govt. Khash land In the Khash Mahal Khatian. The said plot was subsequently settled with one Nagendra Chandra Das of Chittagong town by Khash Mahal Department, now defunct, creating a Jote holding being No. 243 under khatian No.1312/15. The said No. 115 plot was thereafter sold in a certificate sale for arrears of rent and it was auction purchased by the Government and R. S, case No. 563/46-47 was started for re-settlement of the said plot but as there was no application for taking settlement of the same, case No. 165 1951.52 was started for recording the said plot as khash land to the Government khash khatian, being Register No VIII. It was accordingly made khash and it was so entered in Register No. VIII Ext.3) as khash land, at page 88. It was also entered as such in Register No. VI of the Tahshil Office. It was also entered as khash land in Register No. 1 being the settlement libation volume (Ext. II). In the year 1962 on instructions received from the higher authorities the local settlement staff concerned prepared a fresh list of Govt. khash lands situated within the same Mouza after consulting Register No. VII (Ext 3) and also Register No. 1, record of settlement khatian (Ext.11) It was so prepared by P.W.9 Abdul Quddus Tahsilder, Chandgaon Tahshil office and In that newly prepared volume, being Ext. 3/4, plot No. 115 was recorded by him as khash land. Since the new register, Ext. 3/4, as prepared by Abdul Quddus was found clumsy it was ordered by him to be re-written whereupon accused-appellants Aminul Islam and Harish Chandra Das, Assistant Tahshilders, prepared two other copies of the said Register in two other Bound Books, being Exts. 3/2 and 3/3 respectively and at page 84 and 94 in Ext. 3/3 plot No. 115 was recorded as Government khash land and at pages Nos. 87 and 94 In Ext. 3/2 the said land were also recorded as khash land. The entire khash land within Chandgaon, Tahshil Office were again recorded In Ext.6 (in all eleven sheets) by them. This Ext. 6 was finally signed by the accused Asst. Tahshildar Harish Chandra Das on 10.12. 62 verified by the Circle Inspector, Mukhlesur Rahman on 10.1.63 and it was signed and forwarded by the accused appellant Kazi Muzharul Huq, the Sub Divisional Manager on 10.1.63 for onward transmission to the Collector and in that Ext. 6 page 3, plot No 115 was recorded as Government khash land. When this was the position S A. operation started in Chittagong area and during that operation the accused appellant Saleh Ahmed Master became very active and in order to gain pecuniary advantage, dishonestly, in collusion with the other accused appellants be fabricated the original revisional settlement record and the words Misc Case No. 212/ 50-52 and 63/51-52 and the name reading "Saleh Ahmed Master" was inserted by him in the khasara volume (Ext. IX), corresponding to the said S A. khatian, in Dakhaldar" column against plot No, 115, comprising an area of 16 acres, after erasing the original words that existed there. Accused-appellant Saleh Ahmed Master in collusion with the accused-appellant Assistant Tashildar Aminul Islam removed pages NOS. 87 and 94 from Ext 3/3 wherein plot No. 115 was recorded as khash land and Introduced from outside, in the band writing of accused Aminul Islam, new pages 87 and 94 by forgery omitting plot No. 115 from the list of khas land, dishonestly. Accused Asst. Tashildar Harish Chandra Das caused to remove pages 84 and 94 from Ext. 3/2 and introduced by forgery, in the handwriting of accused Harish Chandra new pages from outside, dishonestly, omitting plot No 115 from the list of Government Khash land Accused-Appellant Saleh Ahmed Master by an unregistered patta dated 21-9-38 and some dakhilas, said to have been granted by the original jotder Nagendra Chandra Das in favour of his late father, then got his name entered in the tenants ledger, being Register No. (II Ext. 4) through the pen of P W. 7 Shital Chandra Dey, a peon of Fatikchan Tahshil Office and In collusion with the settlement staff be forged and fabricated the attested copy of the record of right in his own hand inserting the writing reading "Saleh Ahmed Master, Dakhaldar of plot No. 489, (old RS plot No. 115) of khatian No. 1312/ 15 Paschim Soloshahar and on the basis of those entries Tashildar Nirendre Kumar Das received rents from him showing him as owner of R.S. plot No 115 (new plot No 489) by granting rent receipts and thereafter Hafizur Rahman Tahshildar received rents from him on 15.3 61 and the accused-appellant Aminul Islam received rents from him on 3 4.62 dishonestly, though acre were re-cords in the Tahshil Office to show that the plot In question was a Government khash land. On the basis of the said papers and forged entries in various Government records accused Saleh Ahmed Master, thereafter, in collusion with she other accused appellants get his name recorded in the P.R.R khatian illegally and dishonestly. Some time in 1963 the Director of Forest of the then East Pakistan Government, submitted a proposal foe acquisition of R.S. plot No. 115 for establishing a forest college. Consequently L.A. Pre-Case No. 292/63-64 was started and Surveyor, Abdul Khair (P W.8) was asked on 10.6.64 to survey the land, who after due enquiry reported on 22.6 64 that the land was a Government khash land, against which report the accused appellant Saleh Ahmed Master produced all these forged papers in support of his ownership of plot No. 115 whereupon Fazlul Karim Chowdhury, the Land Acquisition Officer referred the matter to the Sub-Divisional Manager (North) Chittagong, namely, accused-appellant Kazi Mozaharul Hoque for confirmation regarding ownership of the land in question and the accused-appellant Kazi Mozaharul Hoque, having full knowledge that the land in question was Government khash land, In turn asked for a report from the accused appellant Sha6qur Rahman, Tahshilder, Chandgaon Tahshil office. The said Talishilder, who had Register No. VIII and other records in his office showing plot No. 115 as lamb land, in order to allow pecuniary benefit to the accused-appellant Saleh Ahmed Master, by misusing his official power and position, submitted a dishonest false report under his memo No. 121 dated 11.7.64 stating, Inter ails, that the land in question was recorded in the name of the accused-appellant, Saleh Ahmed Master and that the said plot No. 115 was not found In register No. VIII and on the basis of the said false and dishonest report, accused-appellant Kazi Mozharul Hoque submitted a false report, dishonestly, to the Land Acquisition Deputy Collector on 16.7.64 stating that the land in question was not khash land and the compensation money could be paid to the accused-appellant, Saleh Ahmed Master being the owner of the land in question. On the basis of the said report, Mr. Fazlul Karim Chowdhury, Land Acquisition Deputy Collector paid 50% compensation money for the acquisition of the said plot No. 115, amounting to Tk. 55,600/- to the accused-appellant Saleh Ahmed Master, through his attorney P.W. 11 on 29.7 64. Some time thereafter this irregularity as to payment of the compensation money to the accused-appellant Saleh Ahmed Master was reported by one Mokbul Ahmed to the Board of Revenue and on a complaint submitted by the Board of Revenue (Ext. 17), the Bureau of Anti-Corruption inquired into the matter and the Anti-Corruption Bureau, after completing enquiry, lodged the F.I.R against the accused appellants on 3.10.68 and Chittagong P.S. case No. 60/68 was started. Police, after investigation, submitted charge-sheet against all the accused appellants under various sections of the Penal Code and under Act II of 1947. After due sanction the C6urt of Special Judge, Chittagong took cognizance in the matter and the accused-appellant Saleh Ahmed Master was put on trial to answer a charge punishable under section 468/4771/471/ 420/109 and under section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act (Act II of 1947.) Accused-appellants Aminul Islam, and Harish Chandra Das were put on trial to answer a common charge punishable under section 467 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of Act II of 1947. Accused appellants Mozharul Hoq and Shafiqur Rahman under 420/109 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of Act II of 1947. 

 4. At the trial the prosecution examined as many as 14 witnesses including the Investigation Officer (P.W. 14) the Hand Wilting Expert (P.W. 10) and provided a large number of official records and official documents to substantiate the prosecution cave. The defence examined none. The defence was a plea of not guilty. Their further case, it appears from the trend of cross-examination of the prosecution witnesses, was that the land under  plot No. 115 was under the Jote settlement of one Nagendra Lal Das who thereafter leased out the said land by executing a petition dated 21-9-39 in favour of the father of the accused-appellant Saleh Ahmed Master and after his death accused appellant Saleh Ahmed Master came to be in possession of She said land and during the preparation of the records of right the disputed land was duly recorded in the settlement khatian in the name of the accused-appellant Such Ahmed Master and as inch the land was not a Government khash land and that the accused-appellant Saleh Ahmed Master, so also the accused appellants Aminul Islam and Harish Chandra Das, never had tampered with any Government records in order to aid or abet the commission of any offence of forgery and fabrication as alleged by the prosecution and that the accused-appellants Kazi Mozaharul Hoque and Shafiqur Rahman submitted the report showing accused-appellant Salon Ahmed Master as owner, of the disputed plot on She basis of records as were available and It was done honestly and bonafide and In the due discharge of their official duties and they in no way caused any pecuniary gain to Saleh Ahmed Master at the expense of the Government, dishonestly misusing their official power and position. It was their further case that the prosecution, having recently manufactured some forged papers and documents for the purpose of this case, has implicated the accused-appellant falsely in this false case. [Discussion of the witnesses entirely omitted] 

 6. In judging the nature of a criminal act of cheating me only thing relevant is the intention of the accused at the time of the inducement when one was induced to part with his property or to act to his detriment which he would not have acted but for the misrepresentation and the consequent inducement. There must exist a dishonest intention to cause wrongful gain and wrongful loss by unlawful means at the time of taking by inducement if no dishonest mind was acting at the time of taking the property or money, the subsequent wrongful action, if any, of a person may amount to a preach of a contract or a civil wrung but not cheating. Mere taking of money or property one day honestly and running away with it the next day is not necessarily an act of cheating. In the instant case, however, the dishonest intention of the accused-appellant Saleh Ahmed to defraud the Government and to cause wrongful gain and wrongful loss by unlawful means became apparent on Moe day when he introduced his name, in his own hand-writing, showing him as owner in possession of Government khash plot No. 115, in the Khaoshra Khatian volume by erasing the original entry and when he proceeded to enter, in his own hand-writing by forgery, his name in the attested copy of the khatian, showing him, as owner of plot No. 115 and forged a patta, said to have been executed in favour of his late father by the original Jutdar in 1938, intending to use it as genuine concerning his title to plot No. 115. All his subsequent acts of tampering with other Government records and inducing other accused-appellants to tamper with Exts 3/2 and 3/3 and inducing the Sub-Divisional Manager and the Tahshilder to submit false and dishonest reports in his favour, showing him as owner of the plot in question were but series of similar acts done in the prosecution of the common object to cheat the Government. His dishonest intention to cheat was put Into action when he dishonestly induced the Government official to act on the basis of the forged entries, forged pattas and dakhilas and false reports and to deliver to him through his attorney P W. 11, a sum of Tk 55,600/- to which he was not entitled under the law, causing a wrongful gain to himself and wrongful loss to the Government. 

 21. We have already seen that the accused-appellant Kazi Mozaharul Hoq, had forwarded Est. 6 under his own signature to the Collector, wherein at page No. 3 R.S. plot No. 115 of west Sholashahar was shown as Government khash land. It has been stated by P.W. 8 Abdul Khair, a surveyor attached to the Land Acquisition Department, Chittagong, that he was asked to survey R S. plot No. 115 as there was a proposal for acquisition of the same and that on examination of the relevant Government records he prepared the land schedule showing the said plot as Government Khash land covering an area of 16,00 acres but against that survey report accused-appellant Sales Ahmed Master filed an objection petition claiming the said land as his own. The report of the Surveyor which was marked as Ext. 26 read thus: 

 "From the District room & Tahsil records it appears that R.S. plot No. 115 of Mouza West Sholashahar bar stands as khash land but one Saleh Ahmed Master, son of Md. Ismail of West Sholashahar produced a copy of the P.S. Khatlan and some rent receipt, in support of his record of right. Verified the record in the State Acquisition Department and Tahshil office it appears that ownership of the said plot of land is yet with the Government vide Commissioner's letter No. 445-R dated 24-3.47 and Deputy Commissioner's letter No. 488 KW dated 28-3-1959". 

 22. On the body of the said report, Dist. Kanungo on 22-6.64 ordered that the matter may be confirmed by the S.D.M. and if it is found to be a Government land the requiring body would be requested to take possession by transfer from the State Acquisition Department. Thereafter, vide memo No. 3583 dated 30.6 64 k Ext. 29) issued from the office of the Deputy Commissioner, Chittagong the Sub-Division Manager, accused appellant Kazi Mozaharul Hoque was requested to examine the matter and to report. The said memo No.3583 dated 30.6.64 as referred to above reads as follows:—"To Sub-Divisional Manager. north Chittagong, Sub Requisition and acquisition of land for establishment of forest college, Sholashahar: Director, East Pakistan Forest College, Chittagong pieced a proposal for requisitioning R.S. plot No. 115 of khatian 983 of west Sholashahar, P.S Panchlaish, Chittagong for establishing forest college, Chittagong but It appeals from R. S. record and surveyor's report that the aforesaid plot is Government Khash land but one Saleh Ahmed Master, son of Md. Ismail of west Sholashahar produced some old rent-receipt and a copy of the R.S. Khatian in support of his claim to the aforesaid plot. You are, therefore requested to furnish this office the full particulars of the ownership of the said plot at an early date." 

 23. From the above It Is apparent that the accused-appellant Kazi Mozaharul Hoque Sub-Divisional Manager, who was already In the know of the fact was again clearly informed by the office of the Deputy Commissioner, Chittagong that the said land was recorded In the Collector's record as Government khash land and that the surveyor after consulting the Tahshil records and Collector record bad found the land as a khash land but vet the accused-appellant Saleh Ahmed was claiming the land as his own. Accused-appellant Kazi Mozaharul Hoque and his Tahshilder accused-appellant Shafiqur Rahman in the facts and circumstance, as relevant by the Collector's letter (Ext. 29), had a clear duty to take such care as was expected of them as public servants before passing their final opinion as to the ownership when the land was also being claimed by the Government. They had a duty to protect Government property from being lost and they being in a position of absolute trust and confidence had a further duty to honour that obligation which they not only dishonestly failed to honour but they In collusion with the accused appellants Saleh Ahmed Master and in prosecution of their common object to cheat and to obtain pecuniary gain for accused-appellant Saleh Ahmed Master, by abusing their official position dishonestly submitted a false report declaring Saleh Ahmed Master as the owner. If P.W.8, the surveyor, and the Office of the Deputy Commissioner could still find plot No. 115 recorded as khash land in various official registers & records it is not understood as to how the accused-appellants Kazi Mozaharul Hoque and Shafiqur Rahman could miss it and overlook their own previous report (Est.6) if it was not a calculated dishonest design on their part to take no notice of that entry as in Ext. 6 and the entries in Vol. VIII (Ext. 30) and the entry in Ext. 3/4 and in other records In order to obtain pecuniary benefit for Saleh Ahmed Master, committing an offence punish-able under section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947. 

 24. On an examination of Ext. 3/4 by us, which Ext. 3/4 is a newly recorded khash land volume, copied from the old register recently by P.W 9 Abdul Quddus, which was again copied by the accused appellant Aminul Islam in another volume (being Ext. 3/2) and by accused-appellant Harish Chandra Das (in Ext. 3/3) it is seen that in Ext. 3/4 at page 103 the khash land plots were recorded one after the other thus :—plot 29,31,31/159, 33/160,4033 and 115 being the last number In that rage but in Ext. 1/3 (which Is a copy of Ext. 3/4) it now stand recorded thus Plot 29,31,31/159.33/160,4033 and 2328/2995 and last plot No. 2328/2995 was newly inserted omitting plot No. 115 keeping the other numbers intact and copied one after the other as it stood originally in Ext. 3/4. In Ext, 3/3 also all those numbers were copied as they stood in Ext, 3/4 one after the other but Inserting plot number 2328/2995 in place of plot number 115 omitting plot number 115 altogether as the last number in that page. We find that the Ext. 3/2 and 3/3 are nothing but verbatim copies of Ext. 3/4. This being so it is not understood as to why plot 115 would be or could be omitted by the accused appellants when they initially copied and it was alleged by the prosecution that those were re-written subsequently, with new page numbers and were inserted from outside omitting plot number 115 as the last entry. P.W. 10, the Hand-writing Expert, proved these entries and the new page number appearing at page 87 and 54 in Ext. 3/3 to be in the hand-writing of accused-appellant Harish Chandra Das and the entry and new page number appearing at pages 85 and 94 in Ext. 3/2 to be in the hand-writing of accused-appellant Aminul Islam. It is thus evident that those newly filled up pages with new page numbers were subsequently written in some blank pages, after removing blank pages from the volume and were subsequently inserted again from outside by the writers themselves, where they dishonestly omitted plot No. 115 from the list of khash land in the manner as discussed herein before We have ourselves examined those and it clearly appeared to us that those were written subsequently in the hand-writing of the accused-appellant Aminul Islam and Harish Chandra Das from where plot No. 115 was omitted. Accused-appellants Aminul Islam and Harish Chandra Das did those dishonestly, in order to give authority to the accused to claim ownership and did these in prosecution of their common object to chart and to obtain pecuniary benefit for the accused Saleh Ahmed Master by abusing their official position and power as public servants thereby committed an offence punishable under section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act II of i 947.
